samples.summary: Commander's raw parse message is copied verbatim into the machine-readable `USAGE` envelope, so a mistyped credential flag (`--api-keyy=sk-live-…`) is serialized into a structured stderr field that agent drivers persist
samples.evidence: Vector: a user/agent mistypes a secret-bearing flag, e.g. `wafflebase docs list --api-keyy=sk-live-ABC123` (or `--apikey=<token>`). Commander v13 (packages/cli/package.json:26) pushes the whole `--flag=value` token into `parsed.unknown` when `_findOption(arg.slice(0, index))` misses, and `unknownOption(flag)` builds `error: unknown option '--api-keyy=sk-live-ABC123'`. cli.ts:87 takes `e.message`, strips only the `error: ` prefix, and hands it to `outputError`, which JSON-stringifies it into `{"error":{"code":"USAGE","message":"unknown option '--api-keyy=sk-live-ABC123'"}}` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:57-62). The same happens for any secret passed as an unrecognized `--x=value`. Note the exposure channel (stderr) is not new — commander printed the identical prose before this change — but the change promotes it from transient prose into the documented structured field that agent drivers are explicitly told to parse and typically log/store (packages/cli/README.md:116-122, docs/design/cli.md:780-800). A cheap hardening would be to truncate the `=<value>` tail of an unknown-option token before enveloping. Severity kept minor because the underlying echo predates the diff and no new sink is introduced; confidence medium because commander is not installed in this tree, so the `--flag=value` message shape is asserted from commander v13 source knowledge rather than executed.
